binders: A real m by n matrix A, represented as entries A_ij for i in Fin m and j in Fin n.
hypotheses: For every row i, r_i := max_{j in Fin n} |A_ij| is strictly positive.
conclusions: For every row i, its scale lambda_i is an integral power of two: there exists e in the integers such that lambda_i = 2^e.
For every row i, lambda_i > 0 and theta/(2r_i) < lambda_i <= theta/r_i.
For every row i and column j, |lambda_i A_ij| <= theta.
For every row i, there exists a column j, which may depend on i, such that theta/2 < |lambda_i A_ij|.
mathematical_definitions: Fin k denotes the index set {0,...,k-1}.
theta = min(fmax, sqrt(Fmax/n)), where n is viewed as a real.
For a row x with r = max_j |x_j|, if theta/r > 0, e(theta,x) is a classically selected integer satisfying 2^e <= theta/r < 2^(e+1); otherwise e(theta,x) = 0.
D = diag(lambda_0,...,lambda_{m-1}) and B = DA, so exactly B_ij = lambda_i A_ij.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every positive-dimensional real matrix A, and every positive pair fmax and Fmax, assume that no row of A is identically zero. Set theta equal to the smaller of fmax and sqrt(Fmax/n). Scale each row i by the integral power of two lambda_i obtained by locating theta/r_i in a half-open interval [2^e,2^(e+1)), where r_i is that row's maximum absolute entry. Then each lambda_i is positive and lies strictly above theta/(2r_i) and at or below theta/r_i. Consequently every entry of the scaled matrix DA has absolute value at most theta, while every scaled row has at least one entry whose absolute value is strictly greater than theta/2.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The declaration applies only when m and n are positive. If either dimension is zero, the corresponding positivity premise is false and the implication is vacuous.
Every row must have positive maximum absolute entry, equivalently every row must contain a nonzero entry. If any row is zero, the row hypothesis fails and the declaration gives no conclusion.
The positivity of fmax, Fmax, and n implies theta > 0; together with r_i > 0 this ensures that D007 always takes its positive branch in this proposition.
Division by n and by r_i is protected by the stated positivity assumptions.
The exponent is an integer, so lambda_i may be a reciprocal power of two; the proposition does not restrict it to powers with nonnegative exponent.
The exponent is introduced by classical choice and no computational algorithm for obtaining it is encoded.
The existential column witnessing theta/2 < |lambda_i A_ij| may be different for each row and is not asserted to be unique.
No relationship between fmax and Fmax is assumed beyond positivity, and they affect the result only through theta.

No floating-point format, rounding operation, overflow behavior, representability condition other than being an integral power of two, error bound, uniqueness claim, columnwise bound, or global matrix-norm statement is encoded.
